generated_by: Hand-written inputs, Python SHA-256, cross-validated with Node.js crypto

categories.body_normalization: body-001 through body-013 (BOM inc. UTF-16 LE/BE, line endings, whitespace, blank lines)
categories.recipient_parsing: rcpt-001 through rcpt-013 (angle brackets, display names, case, order, quoted, comments, comma-in-display-name; rcpt-010+ add raw_headers wire forms: duplicate To instances, interleaved To/Cc, raw display-name, raw quoted local-part)
categories.unicode: unicode-001 through unicode-004 (Czech, emoji, CJK, Arabic RTL)
categories.address_edge_cases: addr-001 through addr-004 (IDN, long local, subdomains, punycode)
categories.subject: subj-001 through subj-007 (whitespace trim, empty, internal whitespace, RFC 2047 UTF-8 B, UTF-8 Q, adjacent encoded-words, duplicate Subject instances)
categories.from_selection: from-001 through from-002 (duplicate From instances, multi-mailbox From: first instance, first mailbox)
categories.end_to_end: e2e-001 through e2e-004 (full pipeline, minimal, truncation, and the cut by code points with U+1F642 before it — body given as a recipe)
categories.parts_manifest: parts-001 through parts-008 + shape-a-001 (v1.3 §9: document-order manifest, container-vs-leaf, rfc822 opaque, kind classification, n-omission, Shape A anchor). Replaces retired v1.2 attach-*/html-*/inline-*/mixed-* vectors.
categories.declared_charset: shape-a-002 through shape-a-007 + parts-009 (§2 text read through the declared charset: ISO-8859-2, windows-1250 and ISO-8859-1, each 8bit and quoted-printable; the leaf carries the exact wire payload in payload_base64 and the text it reads as in text)
categories.declared_charset_every_high_byte: shape-a-008 through shape-a-012 + parts-010 (§2 a legacy single-byte charset is read the way the recipient's client reads it, WHATWG Encoding Standard: every byte 0x80-0xFF under iso-8859-1, latin1 and us-ascii (windows-1252), windows-1250 (its undefined bytes read as U+0081, U+0083, U+0088, U+0090, U+0098) and iso-8859-2; the index data is the single-byte indexes of the WHATWG Encoding Standard)
categories.trim_edges: shape-a-013, shape-a-014 + parts-011 (§2 step 4 trim set: exactly the characters ECMAScript String.prototype.trim removes - U+0009-U+000D, U+0020, U+00A0, U+1680, U+2000-U+200A, U+2028, U+2029, U+202F, U+205F, U+3000, U+FEFF; Python's bare str.strip() also removes U+001C-U+001F and U+0085 and keeps U+FEFF)

vectors.description: UTF-8 BOM (U+FEFF) at start of body must be stripped
U+FEFF not at position 0 must be preserved (zero-width no-break space)
Lone CR (old Mac line endings) must be normalized to LF
CRLF line endings must be normalized to LF
Mixed CRLF + lone CR + LF must all normalize to LF
Trailing spaces and tabs per line must be stripped
Multiple blank lines must NOT be collapsed (C2 regression test)
Empty body string must produce empty body in canonical object
Single character body
Whitespace-only body normalizes to empty string
BOM + CRLF + trailing whitespace combined normalization
UTF-16 LE BOM (bytes FF FE) must be detected at byte level, email decoded to UTF-8, BOM stripped, warning logged. Canonical form is the decoded UTF-8 text without BOM.
UTF-16 BE BOM (bytes FE FF) must be detected at byte level, email decoded to UTF-8, BOM stripped, warning logged. Canonical form is the decoded UTF-8 text without BOM.
Angle bracket addresses must be extracted to bare form
Display names must be stripped, only addr-spec preserved
Email addresses must be lowercased
Recipient order must be preserved (NOT sorted)
Quoted local parts: quotes stripped from local-part for cross-component consistency
RFC 5322 comments in display name area must be stripped
To and Cc recipients are concatenated in order (To first, then Cc)
No recipients produces empty to field

A display name containing a comma must NOT be split — 'Novák, Jan' <jan@x.cz> is one address, not two. A naive split(',') breaks this. Every implementation must produce the same bare address list, which means the split has to be RFC 5322 aware.
vectors.note: raw_to_header simulates a single To header value as delivered to the TB verifier (verify path). The 'to' array simulates the pre-split form used by the signing path (TB compose API already splits per-recipient). Both paths must yield the same canonical_to.

Body exceeding 1MB must be truncated to exactly 1,048,576 characters

expected.note: Hash computed with body truncated to 1,048,576 chars of A

vectors.description: A body over the limit whose character before the cut is outside the BMP: the cut of §2 "Body Size Limit" counts CODE POINTS, so the last code point of the hashed body is U+1F642 and not half of its surrogate pair. The body is given as a RECIPE (body_parts: {literal} and {repeat, count} pieces, the vocabulary of the free-form lab vectors) because a 1 MiB literal does not belong in a vector file.

input.subject: Large
input.body_description: 1,048,575 x A, then U+1F642, then 1,000 x B

expected.note: Hash computed with the body cut to 1,048,576 CODE POINTS, so it ends in U+1F642. A cut by UTF-16 code units — what the three JavaScript implementations did until v1.4.0-beta.11 — ends in the lone high surrogate U+D83D and gives SZZbSt9prFabgploCc76gKAbSsVjFqPCRO7j5rSe9s0=, which is the value this vector exists to keep out.

vectors.description: Duplicate To header instances — ALL instances contribute, in order. raw_headers is the wire form (one [name, value] pair per header line); 'to' is the merged array form a mail API may hand over instead. A reader that joins the instances into one unparseable string, or that keeps only the first or only the last, builds a different canonical object — which is why this vector carries both forms of the same message.
Interleaved To/Cc instances group as ALL To values first, then ALL Cc values — not arrival order.

The RAW wire form of a display-name To. It must canonicalize to the same bare address (and therefore the same content_hash) as rcpt-001's bare form. A stored header value that keeps its trailing line ending can make an address parser return nothing at all, and a fallback split(',') then leaks the display name into the canonical string: trim the value before parsing it.
Quoted local-part in the raw wire form: quotes are stripped identically by all four implementations (stripLocalQuotes / _strip_local_quotes).
Duplicate Subject header instances — the FIRST instance wins, in every implementation. A smuggled second Subject must not reach the canonical hash, and its decode errors must be ignored.
Duplicate From header instances — the FIRST instance wins, in every implementation.

A single From header containing multiple mailboxes — the FIRST mailbox wins, bare and lowercased. An implementation that passes the whole field value through a bare-address extractor instead will not reach this canonical object, and must fail closed rather than guess.
v1.3 #3: TWO text/plain leaves -> two k:plain entries in document order; the second text part is bound (v1.2 covered only the first)
v1.3 #2 injectivity (1/2): plain + html "A" + html "B" as separate leaves
v1.3 #2 injectivity (2/2): plain + ONE html "A\nB" leaf — MUST hash differently from parts-002a (under v1.2 the "\n"-join made them collide)
v1.3 #4 (G2): message/rfc822 is an opaque LEAF — no descent; h = SHA-256 of the entire attached .eml bytes; n = rfc822[0]
